newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 1997 GDP growth seen around 6.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 1997 GDP growth seen around 6.0 pct.

text.p: Philippine gross domestic product (GDP) is expected to grow around six percent this year, the Asia-Pacific director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said at a news conference on Thursday.
"GDP is a little over six percent," IMF director John Hicklin said in reply to a question on whether a lower GDP was expected versus the original forecast of 7.1 to 7.8 percent this year.
The adjusted GDP projections came after the actual 1996 GDP figure of 5.5 percent was announced in late January.

In the same news conference, Philippine Central Bank officials said they expect a lower balance of payments surplus of $2.9 billion at the end of 1997 as against the latest preliminary figure of $4.1 billion at end 1996.
Philippines Airlines' aircraft acquisition programme of $1.1 billion this year will result in a lower balance of payments surplus, officials said.
Consequently, the country's trade deficit this year is expected to widen to $13.8 billion from $11.786 billion in 1996, they said.
The 1997 current account deficit is also seen to widen to 4.2 percent of GNP, or $4.1 billion, compared with a preliminary 4.1 percent in 1996, or $3.6 billion, officials said.
The current account measures non-merchandise and merchandise trade, as well as transfers or donations from abroad.
The balance of payments measures the current account, as well as inflows and outflows of foreign loans and investments.
